limits: Role intervals overlap; do not sum them as elapsed time.
Input and authoring windows are subsets of each invocation.
Native execution supplies no output-stream/command-generation or pure reasoning durations.
Usage snapshots may be cumulative; no additive token or credit claim.
Byte counts cover recorded input payloads and returned text fields, not complete MCP transport bytes.
Latest acceptance can include renderer refresh or later reuse; first acceptance is reported separately.

findings.issue: The rendered initial view places the applied-crop summary and return feedback below the dialog body's visible scroll area. The scrollbar provides access, but the visible content does not immediately confirm the crop change when returning from Source rectangle.
findings.remedy: Consider showing a compact applied-crop confirmation in the visible summary, or specifying return focus and scrolling that bring the existing crop feedback into view.

findings.issue: The committing scene retains Opening cut, an ordinary named clip, but describes its crop as 'full composed frame'; the corresponding named-clip scene describes 'full source frame'. This is a minor inconsistency in staged crop identity.
findings.remedy: Use 'full source frame' for this committing example and reserve 'composed frame' for Scene montage.

findings.issue: The initial Content chooser declares state focus, but the actual screenshot shows only resting option outlines, with no visible focus ring or keyboard-active item. The rendered entry state therefore does not communicate the required keyboard focus location.
findings.remedy: Make the declared Content focus visibly render on the chooser or its keyboard-active option, distinct from selected content. Preserve the initially empty selection and disabled Add, then inspect the corrected screenshot. If the built-in choice-group renderer suppresses this supported state, resolve that preview limitation before visual acceptance.

findings.issue: The committing scene selects Opening cut and identifies an independent named-clip copy, but its crop summary says full composed frame. The corresponding named-clip scene says full source frame. This introduces an inconsistent description of the retained staged crop.
findings.remedy: Use the crop description belonging to the staged Opening cut example; reserve composed-frame wording for the composed-clip example.

findings.issue: Disabled Add renders as pale terracotta, also visible for the conflict and committing commands. The frozen command foundation specifies the neutral disabled-background role #D9D9DE. Availability remains understandable, so this is not a blocking defect.
findings.remedy: Align the preview's disabled contained-command treatment with the frozen neutral background and disabled foreground roles while retaining terracotta for enabled primary commands.

findings.issue: The updated disabled styling also gives the outlined Source rectangle command a solid neutral fill; disabled Cancel in the committing scene has the same treatment. The frozen outlined-command foundation retains the ordinary surface and changes its border and foreground. Availability is clear, so this visual consistency difference is nonblocking.
findings.remedy: Keep disabled outlined commands on the #F7F7FC surface with the frozen disabled border and foreground treatment. Reserve the #D9D9DE disabled fill for contained commands such as Add.

findings.issue: The failure scene renders Retry Update Named Clip with focus, while focusIntent says to focus the failure feedback first. Both the message and retry control are visible, but the artifact leaves unclear whether the depicted focus is the initial failure state or a later keyboard position.
findings.remedy: Clarify the intended failure-focus sequence in focusIntent and align the scene's focus illustration with that sequence. If Retry depicts a later position after the failure feedback receives focus, state that explicitly.

findings.issue: Rechecked in revision 5 and still present: the failure scene renders Retry Update Named Clip with focus, while focusIntent says to focus the failure feedback first. Both remain visible, but the artifact does not clarify whether the illustrated focus is initial failure focus or a later keyboard position.
findings.remedy: Clarify the intended failure-focus sequence in focusIntent and align the scene's focus illustration with that sequence. If Retry depicts a later position after the failure feedback receives focus, state that explicitly.

findings.issue: Disabled Cancel renders with a solid neutral fill, matching the disabled contained Updating command. The frozen outlined-command foundation retains the ordinary surface and changes its border and foreground. The disabled state is clear, so this consistency difference is nonblocking.
findings.remedy: Retain the #F7F7FC surface for disabled outlined Cancel and apply the frozen disabled border and foreground treatment; reserve #D9D9DE fill for the contained Updating command.

findings.issue: The range summary identifies All tracks and the inclusive 00:05–00:15 boundaries, but omits the duration requested by selection-menu-context in the acceptance packet. The scope remains understandable, so this does not block the represented menu actions.
findings.remedy: Include the captured range duration alongside its boundaries, using the project's inclusive-frame duration convention.

findings.issue: Rechecked in revision 6: the range summary identifies All tracks and the inclusive 00:05–00:15 boundaries, but still omits the duration requested by selection-menu-context in the acceptance packet. The scope remains understandable, so this does not block the represented menu actions.
findings.remedy: Include the captured range duration alongside its boundaries, using the project's inclusive-frame duration convention.

findings.issue: The rendered ruler packs 00:00, 00:05, 00:10, 00:15 and 00:20 into one left-aligned text string instead of placing them at their temporal positions. The problem affects the actual trim review: in trim-preview, the grouped clip's End is stated as 00:00:10:00, but its end handle is visibly left of the playhead labeled 00:10. Users cannot reliably relate the reviewed boundaries to the ruler, playhead and clip positions. This is a consequential spatial mismatch for the assigned trim action.
findings.remedy: Place separate time ticks or labels on the shared temporal grid and make clip edges, trim handles and playhead positions agree with those times. Adjust representative timestamps and placements together across the selected, inward-trim, extended-trim and ungrouped scenes so identical times align vertically.

findings.issue: The Add review stages another Scene montage as a second grouped occurrence on Track 2 at 00:00:22:00 after B-roll, and commit-freeze explicitly retains the pre-insertion timeline. No supplied success scene shows that second occurrence. Overview's generic 'Add completed' message accompanies the same original objects already present in the frozen before-state. The successful branch of this assigned action therefore cannot be followed from its reviewed destination to the resulting timeline and selection.
findings.remedy: Provide a corresponding successful Add result showing the new independent grouped occurrence at the confirmed Append destination while preserving the existing objects. Show the resulting selection and updated duration, or identify their concrete handoff, consistently with this addition.

findings.issue: The End handle declares focus, but the rendered preview does not provide a distinct focus indicator beyond the selected group's terracotta edge treatment. The same problem appears on the focused End in trim-extended and focused Start in trim-invalid: the focused boundary cannot be visually distinguished from the other enabled trim handle. This leaves keyboard focus ambiguous on the precise editing targets.
findings.remedy: Render a distinct visible focus treatment on the individual focused trim handle, separate from whole-object selection and the unfocused boundary. Preserve the handle's exact ruler alignment and clip geometry. If the visual template does not render its supported focus state, correct that preview limitation and inspect the updated screenshot before acceptance.

findings.issue: Disabled outlined commands such as Return to playhead and Selection actions render with a solid neutral fill. The frozen outlined-command foundation retains the ordinary surface and changes the border and foreground. Disabled availability is understandable, so this consistency difference is nonblocking.
findings.remedy: Retain the #F7F7FC surface with the frozen disabled border and foreground treatment for outlined commands. Reserve the neutral disabled fill for contained commands such as Play during commit.
